title: Canonical ambient ringed-site pullbacks and section-normalized comparators
statement: Let ell be prime, E a finite extension of Q_ell, f:X→Y and g:Y→Z arbitrary scheme maps, and s a positive finite coefficient exponent or the entire ringed sequence site [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. The sectionwise module direct image for the actual structural constant-section ring map has an exact ordinary left adjoint. There exists a unique direct-image comparison push(fg)≅push(f);push(g) whose value at any module section is restriction along baseComp(f,g).inv. There is likewise a unique identity direct-image comparison given by baseId.inv. The specified adjunction mates define comp and identity; their exact termwise localizations define derivedComp and derivedIdentity. These use the original sites and coefficient sheaves [def-coef-semilinear-system-models], with coefficients in max u (t+1) and independent site object and Hom universes. The definitions and hypotheses are as in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition], [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], [def-pc-kflat-complex], [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves].

source.place: Tags 03D3 and 03EL; sites.tex 03CB; sites-cohomology.tex 06YN, 06YS, 07A4, 0G7E and 0G7D. Specialized construction and proof from the ambient coherence argument.

proof.text: Construct the actual coefficient ring sheaf and direct structural maps on the finite or product sequence site. Sheafification naturality gives vertical compatibility, and naturality in the quotient ring maps gives all horizontal compatibility.

Use the ordinary module pullback existence theorem at independent universes. Additivity follows from the additive right adjoint, and finite colimits from left adjointness. Compare finite pullback with coefficientProEtaleModulePullback to obtain finite limits. For the sequence site construct the direct-image/evaluation comparison sectionwise and apply sequenceModulePullbackEvaluation_isIso to its inverse mate. Underlying section evaluations preserve finite limits at every index and reflect them jointly; this proves simultaneous exactness.

For the direct-image composite, extend equality of the constant-section maps by sheafification. This verifies the coefficient linearity of restriction along the canonical fibre-product comparison, including the same-index vertical comparison in the sequence case. Restriction by the inverse comparison gives the inverse module map; sectionwise equality proves uniqueness. The identity proof uses the same constant-section test and the base-change identity restriction. Form the specified left mates and exact derived functor images; no new assertion of their coherence is made here.

theorem pushComp_existsUnique {X Y Z : Scheme.{t}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (s : Option ℕ) :
    ∃! e : push ell E (f ≫ g) s ≅ push ell E f s ⋙ push ell E g s,
      ∀ (M : Modules ell E X s) (U : Site Z s)
        (m : M.val.obj (op ((base (f ≫ g) s).obj U))),
        (e.hom.app M).val.app (op U) m =
          M.val.map ((baseComp f g s).inv.app U).op m
